title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
abstract: arXiv:2611.24932v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. The theory makes five claims: value is governed by calibration rather than by activity, speed, agreement, or tenure; calibration leaves observable traces in behavioral telemetry; those traces are non-diagnostic on their own, because the fast, low-revision signature of a calibrated expert is indistinguishable from that of a confident novice until it is gated by outcomes; human calibration and a model's self-knowledge are the same construct, so the joint system should defer to whichever agent is better calibrated on each item; and individual calibration is causally identifiable only abov

translated_title: 知道你所知道的：人机认知系统中审阅者价值的特质理论
translated_abstract: 当一个能力强大的模型与一名人类审阅者在同一决策上协作时，什么样的 人类仍然能贡献价值？我们认为这是一个关于单一认知特质的问题——元认知校准：即审阅者的行为信心与其判断的实际正确性之间的一致程度。我们提出一套审阅者价值的特质理论来使其精确化。该理论提出五个论断：价值由校准程度决定，而非由活动量、速度、一致率或资历决定；校准会在行为遥测数据中留下可观测的痕迹；这些痕迹本身并不具有诊断性，因为经过良好校准的专家所呈现的快速、少修改的行为特征，在未经过结果门控之前与自信的新手难以区分；人类的校准与模型的自我认知是同一个构念，因此人机联合系统应在每个条目上服从校准程度更高的那个智能体；个体校准仅能在……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出“元认知校准”（审阅者信心与其判断实际正确性的一致性）是决定人类审阅者在人机协作认知系统中核心价值的唯一关键特质，并主张联合系统应将每个决策条目的最终裁定权交给校准程度更高的智能体——无论是人还是模型。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a trait theory identifying metacognitive calibration—the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and actual correctness—as the key determinant of human reviewer value in human-AI cognitive systems, arguing that the joint system should defer on each item to whichever agent, human or model, is better calibrated.
